literal: Thereupon Liu Yu was first enfeoffed as Duke of Song.
idiomatic: Liu Yu received his first investiture as Duke of Song.

literal: On day Renzi in the sixth month, the Great White moved direct and entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s right Censor Gate.
idiomatic: June, renzi: Venus moved direct into the enclosure’s right rear gate.

literal: On day Jisi, the moon transgressed the Net.
idiomatic: Jisi: the Moon crossed the Net.

literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
idiomatic: Same Net gloss as before.

literal: In the seventh month, the moon transgressed the Ox station.
idiomatic: July: the Moon crossed the Ox lodge.

literal: On day Bingxu in the tenth month, the moon entered the Net.
idiomatic: October, bingxu: the Moon entered the Net.

literal: In the thirteenth year, fifth month, day Bingzi, the moon transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: Thirteenth year, May, bingzi: the Moon crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: On day Dinghai, it transgressed the Oxherd.
idiomatic: Dinghai: the Moon crossed the Oxherd.

literal: On day Guisi, Mars transgressed the Right Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: Guisi: Mars crossed the Right Law Enforcer.

literal: On day Jiyou in the eighth month, the moon transgressed the Oxherd.
idiomatic: August, jiyou: the Moon crossed the Oxherd.

literal: On day Dingmao, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Dingmao: the Moon crossed the Supreme Palace.

literal: The prognostication states: "The ruler will be anxious."
idiomatic: The sovereign faces ill portent.

literal: On day Renchen in the ninth month, Mars transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: September, renchen: Mars crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: On day Wushen in the tenth month, the moon transgressed the Net.
idiomatic: October, wushen: the Moon crossed the Net.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Glosses matched prior entries.

literal: The moon transgressed the Winnowing Basket.
idiomatic: The Moon crossed the Winnowing Basket (Ji).

literal: The prognostication states: "The state will have grief."
idiomatic: National mourning follows.

literal: On day Jiayin, the moon transgressed the Net.
idiomatic: Jiayin: the Moon crossed the Net.

literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
idiomatic: Same Net omen again.

literal: On day Yimao, Saturn transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure and halted, accumulating more than seventy days.
idiomatic: Yimao: Saturn crossed the enclosure and lingered over seventy days.

literal: The prognostication states: "Warning of a lost ruler."
idiomatic: A lost-ruler omen is recorded.

literal: On day Renxu, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Renxu: the Moon crossed the Supreme Palace.

literal: In the fourteenth year, third month, day Guisi, the Great White transgressed the Five Feudal Lords.
idiomatic: Fourteenth year, March, guisi: Venus crossed the Five Feudal Lords.

literal: On day Gengzi in the fifth month, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: May, gengzi: the Moon crossed the Supreme Palace.

literal: On day Jiachen in the seventh month, Mars transgressed the Ghost Cart.
idiomatic: July, jiachen: Mars crossed the Ghost asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "Qin will have arms; moreover drought; moreover arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Qin lands face war, drought, and battlefield death.

literal: It also says: "Great men will grieve; the ancestral temples will change; moreover there will be rebellious ministers."
idiomatic: Magnates mourn, dynastic temples shift, and traitorous ministers appear.

literal: At the time Liu Yu monopolized commands, armies rose repeatedly, famine and drought followed one another, and afterward he finally moved the Jin house.
idiomatic: Liu Yu held absolute power, campaigns and dearth came in waves, and he ultimately transferred the Jin mandate.

literal: On day Dingsi, the moon transgressed the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: Dingsi: the Moon crossed the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "An army general will die."
idiomatic: A field commander will perish.

literal: On day Jiazi in the eighth month, the Great White transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: August, jiazi: Venus crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: On day Guiyou, Saturn entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, transgressed the Right Law Enforcer, and therefore stayed inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure, accumulating more than two hundred days before departing.
idiomatic: Guiyou: Saturn entered the enclosure, crossed the Right Law Enforcer, and lingered inside over two hundred days.

literal: The prognostication states: "When Saturn guards the Supreme Palace Enclosure, it is warning of a lost ruler; there will be a moved king."
idiomatic: Saturn’s long stay in the enclosure marks a dying dynasty and shifting kingship.

literal: On day Yiwei in the ninth month, the Great White entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and transgressed the Left Law Enforcer.
idiomatic: September, yiwei: Venus entered the enclosure and crossed the Left Law Enforcer.

literal: On day Dingsi, the moon entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Dingsi: the Moon entered the Supreme Palace.

literal: The prognostication states: "Great men will grieve."
idiomatic: High lords face mourning.

literal: On day Jiashen in the tenth month, the moon entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: October, jiashen: the Moon entered the Supreme Palace.

literal: On day Guisi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, transgressed the western bastion’s senior commander, then moved direct to inside the left Censor Gate, halted twenty days, then retrograded.
idiomatic: Guisi: Mars entered the enclosure, struck the western commander star, advanced to the left rear gate, stopped twenty days, then turned retrograde.

literal: In the twelfth Yixi year’s seventh month, Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Hong.
idiomatic: Yixi twelve, July: Liu Yu attacked Later Qin’s Yao Hong.

literal: In the thirteenth year’s eighth month, he captured Yao Hong; Si, Yan, Qin, and Yong were all pacified.
idiomatic: Thirteenth year, August: Yao Hong was taken and Si, Yan, Qin, and Yong were subdued.

literal: In the fourteenth year, Liu Yu returned to Pengcheng and received the title Duke of Song.
idiomatic: Fourteenth year: Liu Yu came back to Pengcheng and took the Song dukedom.

literal: In the eleventh month, Left Director and former general Liu Muzhi died.
idiomatic: November: Liu Muzhi, left director and ex-general, died.

literal: The next year, western barbarians raided Chang’an; the hosts of Yong Inspector Zhu Lingshi were lost; the royal army abandoned it and moved east.
idiomatic: Next year western foes struck Chang’an, Zhu Lingshi’s Yongzhou army was swallowed, and court forces abandoned the city for the east.

literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: December: the emperor died.

literal: In Emperor Gong’s first Yuanxi year, first month day Bingwu, third month day Renyin, and fifth month day Bingshen, the moon each transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure; the prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Yuanxi one: the Moon crossed the Supreme Palace on bingwu, renyin, and bingshen with the usual enclosure glosses.

literal: On day Yimao, Mercury transgressed the Coachman.
idiomatic: Yimao: Mercury crossed Xuanyuan.

literal: On day Gengchen in the sixth month, the Great White transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: June, gengchen: Venus crossed the Supreme Palace.

literal: On day Jimao in the seventh month, the moon transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and the Great White was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: July, jimao: the Moon crossed the enclosure while Venus shone by day.

literal: From the first Yixi year to this time, the Great White crossed the sky nine times; there were four solar eclipses; all began from above; these are images of dynastic change and replacement of kings, ministers losing their ruler.
idiomatic: From Yixi one onward Venus transited the full heavens nine times and four eclipses began at the top—omens of usurpation, fallen kings, and ministers overpowering their sovereign.

literal: That night, the Great White transgressed the Weeping star.
idiomatic: That very night Venus crossed the Weeping star.

literal: On day Dingsi in the twelfth month, the moon and the Great White both entered the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: December, dingsi: Moon and Venus entered the Feathered Forest together.

literal: On day Gengwu in the second year’s second month, Saturn transgressed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Year two, February, gengwu: Saturn crossed the Supreme Palace.

literal: The prognostications were all the same as above.
idiomatic: Same enclosure glosses repeated.

literal: In the first year’s seventh month, Liu Yu received the title Prince of Song.
idiomatic: First year, July: Liu Yu took the Song princedom.

literal: In that year’s sixth month, the emperor abdicated in favor of Song.
idiomatic: That June the emperor yielded the throne to Song.

literal: Broom stars and guest stars
idiomatic: Anomalous broom stars and guest stars

literal: In Wei Emperor Wen’s third Huangchu year, ninth month, day Jiachen, a guest star appeared inside the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s left Censor Gate.
idiomatic: Wei Huangchu three, ninth month, jiachen: a guest star shone inside the enclosure’s left rear gate.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a guest star exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the state will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: A guest star leaving the enclosure foretells war and state funerals.

literal: In the tenth month, the emperor campaigned south against Sun Quan.
idiomatic: October: the emperor marched south against Sun Quan.

literal: After this, there were repeated campaigns and levies.
idiomatic: Endless conscription followed.

literal: In the sixth year, tenth month, day Yiwei, there was a broom star in Shao Wei; it passed through the Coachman; the prognostication: "It is arms and mourning; an image of removing the old and spreading the new."
idiomatic: Year six, October, yiwei: a broom star blazed through Shao Wei and Xuanyuan; gloss—war, mourning, and regime renewal.

literal: At the time the emperor’s army was at Guangling; on day Xinchou he personally donned armor and reviewed the troops.
idiomatic: The host lay at Guangling; on xinchou the sovereign inspected the troops in mail.

literal: In the fifth month of the next year, the emperor died.
idiomatic: Next year’s May: the emperor died.

literal: In Mingdi’s sixth Taihe year, eleventh month, day Bingyin, there was a broom star in the Wings, near the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s senior commander star.
idiomatic: Wei Mingdi Taihe six, November, bingyin: a broom star appeared in the Wings beside the enclosure’s commander star.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is arms and mourning."
idiomatic: War and funerals are portended.

literal: Gan Shi states: "In whatever state a broom or comet strikes, that state receives its disaster."
idiomatic: Gan Shi warns that comets punish the realm they touch.

literal: The Wings are also Chu’s field allotment, the territory Sun Quan enfeoffed.
idiomatic: The Wings mark Chu, Sun Quan’s domain.

literal: The next year, Quan suffered defeat in Liaodong.
idiomatic: The following year Sun Quan met disaster in Liaodong.

literal: The year after that, Zhuge Liang entered the Qin riverlands.
idiomatic: The next year Zhuge Liang advanced into the Qin valleys.

literal: Sun Quan raised troops, along the Yangzi and Huai garrisoned the choke points; Quan himself besieged Xincheng in answer to Liang; the Son of Heaven campaigned east against Quan.
idiomatic: Sun Quan mobilized along the Yangzi and Huai, personally besieged Xincheng to aid Zhuge Liang, while the Wei emperor marched east against him.

literal: In the fourth Qinglong year, tenth month, day Jiashen, there was a broom star at the Great Chen, three feet long.
idiomatic: Qinglong four, October, jiashen: a three-foot broom star appeared at the Great Chen.

literal: On day Yiyou, there was again a broom in the east.
idiomatic: Yiyou: another eastern broom star.

literal: In the eleventh month, day Jihai, a comet appeared, transgressing the eunuch and Celestial Tally stars.
idiomatic: November, jihai: a comet crossed the eunuch and Celestial Tally stars.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Great Chen is the Celestial King; under Heaven there will be mourning."
idiomatic: The Great Chen is the royal seat; the realm faces mourning.

literal: Liu Xiang’s "Treatise on the Five Eras" states: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a star broomed the east and no lodge was named, it means a lodge was not added."
idiomatic: Liu Xiang’s Five Eras treatise notes that unnamed eastern comets omit explicit lodge tags.

literal: Eunuchs are in the Celestial Market; it means inner and outer will have arms.
idiomatic: Eunuch stars sit in the Celestial Market, signaling war inside and out.

literal: The Celestial Tally means earthquake; brooms and comets govern arms and mourning.
idiomatic: The Celestial Tally star signals earthquakes; comets and brooms still mean war and mourning.

literal: In the first Jingchu year’s sixth month, there was an earthquake.
idiomatic: Jingchu one, June: an earthquake struck.

literal: In the ninth month, Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia.
idiomatic: September: Wu’s Zhu Ran ringed Jiangxia.

literal: Empress Mao died.
idiomatic: Empress Mao passed away.

literal: In the second year’s first month, they campaigned against Gongsun Wenyi.
idiomatic: Year two, first month: expedition against Gongsun Wenyi.

literal: In the third year’s first month, Mingdi died.
idiomatic: Third year, first month: Emperor Ming died.

literal: In Jingchu second year, eighth month, a comet appeared in Zhang, three feet long, moving retrograde west, and was extinguished after forty-one days.
idiomatic: Jingchu two, August: a three-foot comet in Zhang moved west retrograde and vanished after forty-one days.

literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
idiomatic: Same comet gloss as prior entries.

literal: Zhang is the field allotment of Zhou.
idiomatic: Zhang marks the Zhou celestial field.

literal: In the tenth month, day Guisi, a guest star appeared in Rooftops, moving retrograde, north of the Detached Palace and south of Coiled Serpent.
idiomatic: October, guisi: a guest star shone in Rooftops, retrograde between the Detached Palace and Coiled Serpent.

literal: On day Jiachen, it transgressed the Ancestral star.
idiomatic: Jiachen: it crossed the Ancestral star.

literal: On day Jiyou, it was extinguished.
idiomatic: Jiyou: it vanished.

literal: The prognostication states: "Wherever a guest star appears there will be arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Guest stars bring war and death to their station.

literal: Emptiness and Rooftops are the ancestral temple; they are also tombs.
idiomatic: Void and Rooftops mark the dynastic shrine and burial ground.

literal: A guest star near the Detached Palace means the palace will soon have great mourning, an image of joining the former lords in the ancestral temple.
idiomatic: Near the Detached Palace it foretells deep palace mourning, as though the ruler were joining his ancestors.

literal: In the third year’s first month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: Third year, first month: the emperor died.

literal: In the Young Emperor’s first Zhengshi year, tenth month, day Yiyou, a comet appeared in the west, in the Tail, three rods long, brushing the Oxherd and transgressing the Great White.
idiomatic: Zhengshi one, October, yiyou: a western comet in the Tail, three rods long, swept the Oxherd and crossed Venus.

literal: In the eleventh month, day Jiazi, it advanced and transgressed the Feathered Forest.
idiomatic: November, jiazi: the comet advanced into the Feathered Forest.

literal: The prognostication states: "The Tail is Yan and also Wu; the Ox is also Wu and Yue’s division."
idiomatic: The Tail marks Yan and Wu; the Ox marks Wu-Yue.

literal: The Great White is the senior commander; the Feathered Forest is central-army troops.
idiomatic: Venus is the commander star; the Feathered Forest is palace guards.

literal: It means Wu and Yue will have mourning and central-army troops will move.
idiomatic: Wu-Yue face funerals while household regiments stir.

literal: In the second year’s fifth month, Wu dispatched three generals to raid the border.
idiomatic: Year two, May: Wu sent three generals to strike the frontier.

literal: Wu heir Deng died.
idiomatic: Wu crown prince Sun Deng died.

literal: In the sixth month, the August Lord campaigned against Zhuge Ke at Wan.
idiomatic: June: Sima Yi attacked Zhuge Ke at Wan.
